Built-in tools cover basic voice input, while dedicated AI tools add personalization, custom vocabulary, and context-aware formatting.

-


Our top-ranked dictation tool for professionals reports ~200ms latency and 98%+ accuracy, with native Mac, Windows, and iOS apps that share the same features.


-


That same pick adds shared team dictionaries and admin controls, supports SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA-compliant workflows, and offers a free plan with no word cap.


## What Is Voice Dictation Software for Your Computer?


Voice dictation software for Mac and Windows converts spoken words into text in real time. Press a hotkey, speak, and your words appear in whatever app you're using: Gmail, Slack, Google Docs, ChatGPT, or anything else. This guide covers live dictation tools only, not meeting transcription services like Otter.ai or Fireflies.[Willow's iOS app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/willow-dictation-ai-keyboard/id6753057525) brings dictation to your iPhone, with vocabulary syncing across Mac, Windows, and iOS. Professionals managing carpal tunnel or ADHD benefit most; see our guide to[voice dictation for neurodivergent workflows](https://willowvoice.com/blog/voice-dictation-reduce-cognitive-load-adhd) .


### How to Choose the Right Dictation Software


-


**Platform:** Look for native Mac or Windows support, not virtualization workarounds.


-


**Accuracy:** Custom vocabulary matters most for technical, medical, or legal terms.


-


**Latency:** Target under ~300ms for fluid, real-time use.


-


**Privacy:** Look for SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance for sensitive data.


-


**App coverage:** Choose a system-wide hotkey over a limited browser extension.

Wispr Flow lists SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and ISO 27001 compliance on its privacy page, with a signed BAA available from its Growth plan. Willow's zero data retention and SOC 2 Type II apply by default on all tiers, and Willow runs natively on Mac and Windows, plus iOS.

## Dragon Professional


Dragon's desktop software is Windows-only, but Nuance also offers cloud-based and medical versions with broader reach. After Nuance discontinued its native Mac desktop version in 2018, Mac users can access Dragon through virtualization software like Parallels Desktop or VMware Fusion, or via Dragon Medical One, a cloud-hosted version that runs through web browsers on Mac and Windows.


Dragon's strengths are deep legal, medical, and business vocabularies and custom voice commands. The tradeoffs are extensive setup and training to reach peak accuracy, a steeper learning curve than plug-and-play tools, virtualization friction for Mac users, and a one-time license of about $699 for Windows.


## Apple Built-in Dictation


Apple's native dictation feature comes pre-installed on macOS and integrates with the system's accessibility framework. Press the Function (Fn) key twice to activate Siri-powered transcription across any text field.


It is free and can run on-device on supported Macs (check[Apple's Dictation settings](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/use-dictation-mh40584/mac) for availability). There is no custom vocabulary editor or filler-word removal, so technical terms need manual correction, and it does not extend to Windows. Best for casual Mac use.


## Windows Voice Typing (Built-in)


Windows 11 includes a free built-in voice typing feature that works in any text field across the operating system. Press Win + H to open the voice typing toolbar, then click the microphone to start speaking. A separate Voice Access mode adds hands-free PC control, letting you move through apps, open menus, and interact with the desktop entirely by voice.


It is free, adds auto-punctuation, and works in most Windows text fields. It has no custom vocabulary editor, filler-word removal, or context-aware formatting, and it requires internet, so it suits occasional use. For a full breakdown, see our guide to[Windows dictation software](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-dictation-software-windows) .


## Microsoft Word Voice Typing


Microsoft Word Voice Typing is built into Microsoft 365 (Word, Outlook, OneNote, and PowerPoint), free for all Microsoft 365 subscribers, and activated via the Dictate button in the Home ribbon or the keyboard shortcut Alt plus backtick on Windows.


It adds 30+ languages, auto-punctuation, and basic commands like "new line" and "delete that" at no extra cost. It does not work in Gmail, Slack, Notion, or other third-party tools, and it has no custom vocabulary or filler-word removal, so it fits people who write only in Word and Outlook.


## Google Docs Voice Typing


Google's browser-based voice typing works in Google Workspace applications through the Chrome browser. Access it through Tools > Voice typing in Google Docs, then click the microphone icon to start speaking.


It is free with a Google account and supports multiple languages plus basic commands like "period" and "new paragraph." It is not system-wide, so it does not reach Gmail or native desktop apps, and it has no custom vocabulary or filler-word removal. It needs internet and suits Google Workspace users who stay in Chrome.


## Voice In Browser Extension


Voice In is a Chrome extension that adds speech-to-text to web apps and forms. Its[Chrome Web Store listing](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/voice-in-voice-typing-spe/pjnefijmagpdjfhhkpljicbbpicelgko) describes dictation in 50+ languages with a free plan for core voice typing. We have not benchmarked its accuracy.


Voice In works in Chrome web apps and forms with a free tier, custom voice commands, and automatic punctuation. Its browser-based architecture excludes native desktop apps, custom vocabulary and formatting controls are limited, and there is no context-aware cleanup or filler-word removal.


## Superwhisper


Superwhisper is one of the more privacy-focused[speech recognition software options](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-speech-recognition-software) , offering on-device and offline transcription for privacy-focused workflows.


Superwhisper runs local models on Mac, Windows, and iOS, so audio stays on-device and works offline, and custom vocabulary is included in the free local plan. Users pick between smaller, faster local models and larger, more accurate ones, trading speed for accuracy. Larger models can add latency on older hardware, and AI cleanup and context-aware modes require Pro. Best for: privacy-conscious users comfortable with local model setup.


**How Willow compares.** Both hold SOC 2 Type II and support HIPAA-compliant workflows with signed BAAs. Willow runs at ~200ms in cloud mode and also offers Offline Mode on Mac and iOS, while Superwhisper averaged about 700ms on 10-60 second dictations in our September 2026 testing.


**Pricing:** A free local tier covers on-device transcription, and paid Pro tiers add larger models and AI modes.


## Wispr Flow


Wispr Flow offers AI dictation on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, with real-time filler-word removal, grammar refinement, and automatic language switching. It also includes Notetaker for meetings on Mac and Windows, with limited access on the free plan. The free desktop plan caps dictation at about 2,000 words per week, and shared team dictionaries require a paid plan. The desktop app is built on Electron, which generally uses more memory than a native app, and its latency in our September 2026 testing was about 900ms at average dictation length (400ms for short dictations). Best for: users who want AI polish across Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android.


**Pricing:** A free tier, with[Pro at $12 per month](https://wisprflow.ai/pricing) billed annually ($15 billed monthly). Wispr Flow lists HIPAA support across all plans, so confirm BAA terms and current pricing on its pricing page.

Yes. Willow Voice runs as a native app with full feature parity on Mac, Windows, and iOS. Custom vocabulary syncs automatically across all three, so terms you add on one device appear on the others without extra configuration.

Willow Voice fits AI-assisted development workflows well, with codebase auto-tagging in Cursor and Windsurf that reads open project files to learn class, function, and variable names. One hotkey works across every IDE and terminal, so you never switch tools to dictate.


### Is speech to text software free and accurate enough for professional use?


Willow's free plan is genuinely unlimited with no word cap. Paid plans add faster, more accurate dictation plus unlimited Willow Scribe. Reported accuracy is 98%+ for Willow versus 85-95% for built-in tools, but treat these figures as indicative, not guaranteed. Test with your own vocabulary and microphone, and review names and numbers before sharing output.

It works inside EHR interfaces like Epic and Cerner without direct integration. Confirm your required agreements and review output before relying on it.
